Many years ago, MacBooks included a slot that allowed you to attach a cable lock to secure the computer to a desk leg or similar fixture. This design was most useful in coffee shops — when you wanted to head back to the counter for another drink, you didn't have to carry your laptop with you.

That slot has long disappeared, but you can now buy an adapter to add a cable lock to your MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, or MacBook Pro……

Users who remember MacBooks with built-in security slots on the side should count themselves as seasoned users. Those slots were designed for T-bar locks: you insert the lock into the slot and rotate it 90 degrees to secure it. The most common design is a cable loop that can pass through a desk leg in a coffee shop or library.

CompuLock has now revived this concept, releasing adapters that mount to the corner or edge of a MacBook so you can attach a cable lock. The adapter uses a two-piece design that clamps onto the MacBook with screws.

The company has now added a MacBook Neo version alongside the existing MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models.

It's important to stress that these locks have always been very low-security devices — their only purpose is to stop someone from grabbing your MacBook and making a run for it during the few seconds you're away. I've used one myself in a small coffee shop and found it acceptable — I could still see my table when I went to the counter for another tea; but if my MacBook was going to be out of my line of sight, I would never rely on one of these locks.

These adapters are priced at $70, which isn't cheap — and you still have to buy the lock itself separately — but if you happen to have a spare lock sitting in a drawer, it might be worth bringing it back into service.
